findings.citation: 7. **Don't change existing contracts.** ... deleted rooms are not listed, not found by name and not joinable
findings.description: Probes check GET /rooms, GET /rooms/:name and /tokens for deleted rooms, but never check that GET /admin/rooms hides tombstones. The oracle's getAllRooms returns tombstones, so the oracle does not follow this sentence for the admin list. No check catches that.

findings.citation: Re-creating a deleted room's name through the existing create endpoints must work and must win over the old tombstone.
findings.description: Only POST /rooms/public is exercised, in the recreate and preserve scenarios. POST /rooms and POST /admin/rooms are untested.

findings.citation: Every local create, update or delete stamps the room with a fresh `updated_at_ms`.
findings.description: Only the access_code edit (PUT) and delete are probed. Renaming a room (PUT name) and enabled toggles are not tested. In the oracle a rename does not tombstone the old name, so it does not replicate cleanly. It can also hit a UNIQUE violation on a tombstoned name.

findings.citation: Records may carry extra fields; peers ignore fields they don't know.
findings.description: No crafted snapshot contains an unknown field, so the checks do not distinguish ignoring extensions from incorporating or rejecting them.

findings.citation: POST /sync/rooms with body {"rooms": <peer snapshot>} (a bare array is also accepted):
findings.description: All successful imports use the object wrapper; the guard scenario only tests malformed objects, never a bare array.

findings.citation: No DNS, no compose, no client work and **no background scheduler**: a future scheduler will simply `GET` a peer's snapshot and `POST` it to the other side on an interval, in both directions.
findings.description: The scenario-only verifier has no check that the submission avoids a scheduler or other out-of-scope runtime work.

findings.citation: Records may carry extra fields; peers ignore fields they don't know.
findings.description: The checks also never verify that unknown fields are excluded from deterministic tie-breaking; this matters because differing peer extensions must not change the winner.

findings.citation: Re-creating a deleted room's name through the existing create endpoints must work and must win over the old tombstone.
findings.description: Only POST /rooms/public is used for resurrection. The authenticated POST /rooms and POST /admin/rooms resurrection paths are not checked.

findings.citation: The existing room, token and admin endpoints keep their behavior: deleted rooms are not listed, not found by name and not joinable; duplicate live names are still rejected with `409`.
findings.description: Coverage omits several existing contracts, including authenticated room creation, admin room creation, regenerate-code, session-history rejoin, repeated deletion, and the admin-list view after deletion.

findings.citation: The existing room, token and admin endpoints keep their behavior: deleted rooms are not listed, not found by name and not joinable; duplicate live names are still rejected with `409`.
findings.description: The oracle's getAllRooms query includes tombstone rows, so GET /admin/rooms lists deleted rooms even though deletion previously removed them and the instruction says deleted rooms are not listed. The hidden checks inspect only the public listing after deletion.

findings.citation: The existing room, token and admin endpoints keep their behavior: deleted rooms are not listed, not found by name and not joinable; duplicate live names are still rejected with `409`.
findings.description: The oracle treats an enabled=0, deleted=false room as absent in duplicate checks and createRoom revives any existing row, so creating the same live-but-disabled name returns success rather than 409. No check attempts this against the legacy disabled room.

findings.citation: Build a bidirectional room-registry sync between two API instances (peers) that stays correct under those conditions.
findings.description: The existing admin API can rename a room, but the oracle changes the natural key in place without emitting a tombstone for the old name. If the old name was already replicated, synchronization retains both old and new names. The preservation check exercises rename only on one backend and never synchronizes it.

findings.citation: Keep the merge/reconcile logic pure and decoupled from HTTP and SQLite where you can; the HTTP and store layers should be thin adapters.
findings.description: All checks are black-box HTTP scenarios and do not verify purity or layer separation.

publicationScope: Admission judgments and native outcome metadata only; prompts, raw streams, HTTP bodies, configuration and credential state excluded.
